newsitem.title: CHINA: CITIC Pac says won't sell Cathay stake.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pac says won't sell Cathay stake.

text.p: CITIC Pacific Ltd's managing director, Henry Fan, denied rumours that the company would unload its 25 percent stake in Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd.
"This 25 percent is for long-term investment and we have no intention to sell," Fan told Reuters on Friday.
"And also we never talk with anybody about the possibility of selling part or all of our stake in Cathay," he said.
Brokers said there were renewed rumours in the market that CITIC Pacific would sell down its interest in Cathay, possibily to China National Aviation Corp (CNAC).
CITIC Pacific shares were up HK$0.70 to HK$47.30 on Friday afternoon, retreating from a morning high of HK$47.80.
Cathay shares rose HK$0.35 to HK$15.10.
"CITIC Pacific has representatives on the board and the executive committee and participates in Cathay's decision making all-round since we increased our stake in Cathay," Fan said.
Fan, who is also the deputy chairman of Cathay, said CITIC Pacific and Cathay's 43.97-percent parent Swire Pacific Ltd were on good terms.
"In fact, our aim is to discuss with the Swire group to further expand Cathay's businesses," he said. "So we have no intention to sell."
Fan also said there were no external pressure that would force the company to sell its Cathay shares.
